intro: Beaches, sunsets, kayaking and nights out on Tito's Lane: Goa backpacking trips made for making new friends.
content:
## Why go to Goa
Goa is India's favourite beach state, and for good reason. North Goa brings the buzz with busy beaches, markets and nightlife, while South Goa slows things down with quieter shores and long sunsets. Add Portuguese-era churches, colourful old neighbourhoods, seafood shacks and water activities, and you have a trip that works whether you want to party, relax or explore. It is also one of the easiest places in India to travel with a group of new friends.

## Best time to visit
November to February is peak season, with pleasant, dry weather and the beaches at their liveliest. March to May gets hot and humid but is quieter. The monsoon, roughly June to September, turns Goa lush and green, though many beach shacks close and the sea gets rough.

## How to reach
Goa has two airports, Dabolim and Mopa (Manohar International Airport), with flights from most Indian cities. Madgaon and Thivim are the main railway stations, and Goa is a popular road trip from Pune and Bangalore.

## Our Goa trips
Our **Goa** backpacking trip is a 4 nights / 5 days road trip starting from ₹11,499 per person. It departs from Pune and Bangalore and covers both halves of the state: a small hike to Cabo de Rama beach, kayaking, sunset at Dona Paula, a hike to the lake near Arambol beach with time for a dip and market shopping, and an evening out at a casino or Tito's Lane (entry fees extra). Trips run every Friday, and groups usually have anywhere from 8 to 50 travellers, with many joining solo.

faqs.q: What is the best time to visit Goa?
faqs.a: November to February is the most popular time, with dry, pleasant weather and a lively vibe. The monsoon months are green and quiet but not ideal for beach time.

faqs.q: How many days are enough for Goa?
faqs.a: Four to five days lets you see both North and South Goa without rushing. Our Goa trip is 4 nights / 5 days.

faqs.q: Is Goa good for solo travellers?
faqs.a: Yes. Goa is one of the most solo-friendly destinations in India, and many travellers join our group trips on their own and leave with a new gang of friends.

faqs.q: Where does the Travel Devils Goa trip start from?
faqs.a: Our Goa backpacking trip is a road trip that departs from Pune and Bangalore, starting from ₹11,499 per person.

faqs.q: What should I pack for Goa?
faqs.a: Light cotton clothes, swimwear, sunscreen, sunglasses, flip-flops and a pair of comfortable shoes for the short hikes. Carry a light rain layer if you travel close to the monsoon.

intro: Shikara rides on Dal Lake, meadows of Gulmarg and Pahalgam, and a night on a houseboat: Kashmir group trips from Delhi.
content:
## Why go to Jammu & Kashmir
Kashmir has been called paradise on earth for centuries, and one look at the valley explains why. Srinagar's Dal Lake, with its shikaras and houseboats, is unlike anywhere else in India. Around it lie meadows and valleys that change completely with the seasons: Gulmarg with its snow and gondola, Sonamarg at the gateway to the high mountains, and Pahalgam along the Lidder river with Betaab Valley and Aru Valley close by. Throw in Mughal gardens, kahwa and wazwan, and it is a trip you will talk about for years.

## Best time to visit
April to June brings spring blooms and pleasant days, ideal for sightseeing. Autumn, around September to November, paints the valley gold with chinar leaves. December to February is snow season, perfect if you want Gulmarg under a white blanket, but expect cold days.

## How to reach
Srinagar airport is well connected to Delhi and other major cities. Jammu is the main railhead, and from there the drive to Srinagar runs through the mountains. Many travellers from North India start with an overnight journey from Delhi to Jammu.

## Our Kashmir trips
Our **Kashmir** backpacking trip is 5 nights / 6 days, starting from ₹22,499 per person. It begins with a sleeper AC bus from Delhi to Jammu and then heads to Srinagar, with day trips to Gulmarg and Sonamarg, a visit to Pahalgam covering Aru Valley, Betaab Valley and Chandanwari, a one-hour shikara ride and a night on a houseboat in Srinagar. Trips run every Friday, with groups usually between 8 and 50 travellers, many of them solo.

faqs.q: What is the best time to visit Kashmir?
faqs.a: Spring (April to June) and autumn (September to November) are great for sightseeing, while December to February is the time to go for snow.

faqs.q: How many days do I need for Kashmir?
faqs.a: Five to seven days is enough to cover Srinagar, Gulmarg, Sonamarg and Pahalgam. Our Kashmir trip is 5 nights / 6 days.

faqs.q: Is the Kashmir trip good for first-timers and solo travellers?
faqs.a: Yes. The itinerary covers the classic highlights, and many of our travellers join solo and travel with the group from Delhi.

faqs.q: What is included in the sightseeing?
faqs.a: The trip covers Srinagar, Gulmarg, Sonamarg and Pahalgam, including Aru Valley, Betaab Valley and Chandanwari, a one-hour shikara ride and a houseboat stay.

faqs.q: What should I pack for Kashmir?
faqs.a: Layers for every season, since mornings and evenings are cool even in summer. In winter, carry a heavy jacket, thermals, gloves, a woollen cap and waterproof shoes.

intro: High passes, Pangong Lake, Nubra's sand dunes and the border village of Turtuk: Ladakh backpacking trips for the ultimate mountain adventure.
content:
## Why go to Ladakh
Ladakh is a high-altitude cold desert that feels like another planet. Think barren brown mountains, deep blue skies, whitewashed monasteries and prayer flags fluttering on some of the highest motorable roads in the world. Nubra Valley surprises you with sand dunes and double-humped Bactrian camels at Hunder, Pangong Lake shifts through shades of blue, and Turtuk offers a glimpse of Balti village life near the border. It is a bucket-list trip for road trippers, bikers and anyone who loves big landscapes.

## Best time to visit
May to September is the main travel season, when the roads are open and days are pleasant. Nights stay cold even in summer. Winter is extremely cold and many high routes close.

## How to reach
Leh airport (Kushok Bakula Rimpochee Airport) has direct flights from Delhi and a few other cities, and is the easiest way in. Leh is also reached by road via Manali or Srinagar during the summer months. Flying in means arriving straight at high altitude, so a day of rest to acclimatise is essential.

## Our Ladakh trips
Our **Leh to Leh** backpacking trip is 6 nights / 7 days, starting from ₹18,999 per person. It begins and ends in Leh, with a first day kept for acclimatisation, then Leh sightseeing, Nubra Valley with Hunder and Diskit Monastery, the village of Turtuk and the Thang viewpoint, and Pangong Lake. There is also a biking option with a rented bike for the Leh to Leh circuit. Trips run every Friday, and groups usually have 8 to 50 travellers, with plenty of solo joiners.

faqs.q: What is the best time to visit Ladakh?
faqs.a: May to September, when the roads are open and the weather is pleasant during the day. Nights are cold throughout the year.

faqs.q: How many days do I need for Ladakh?
faqs.a: About a week is ideal, including a rest day for acclimatisation in Leh. Our Leh to Leh trip is 6 nights / 7 days.

faqs.q: Is Ladakh suitable for first-timers?
faqs.a: Yes, as long as you take acclimatisation seriously. Rest on the first day, stay hydrated and avoid exertion early on. If you have any medical condition, consult your doctor before travelling to high altitude.

faqs.q: Can I do the Ladakh trip on a bike?
faqs.a: Yes. Our Leh to Leh trip has a biking option that includes bike rent for the circuit.

faqs.q: What should I pack for Ladakh?
faqs.a: Warm layers, a windproof jacket, thermals for the nights, sunscreen, sunglasses, lip balm and sturdy shoes. The sun is strong at altitude even when the air is cold.

intro: Living root bridges, Cherrapunji's waterfalls and the clear waters of Dawki: Meghalaya backpacking trips into the abode of clouds.
content:
## Why go to Meghalaya
Meghalaya, the abode of clouds, is one of the greenest corners of India. The state is famous for its living root bridges, grown over generations by the Khasi people, including the double decker root bridge at Nongriat. Cherrapunji (Sohra) is packed with dramatic waterfalls like Nohkalikai and Seven Sisters, Laitlum Canyon offers huge views over the hills, and Dawki's Umngot river is known for water so clear boats appear to float. Mawlynnong, often called one of the cleanest villages in Asia, completes the picture.

## Best time to visit
October to April is a good window for sightseeing, with clearer skies and comfortable weather, and September to December is especially lovely after the rains. The monsoon, roughly June to September, is when the waterfalls are at their fullest, but expect heavy rain and slippery trails.

## How to reach
Guwahati in Assam is the main gateway, with Lokpriya Gopinath Bordoloi International Airport and a major railway station. From Guwahati, Shillong is a scenic drive past Umiam Lake.

## Our Meghalaya trips
Our **Meghalaya** backpacking trip is 5 nights / 6 days, starting from ₹22,499 per person, and runs Guwahati to Guwahati. You drive to Shillong via Umiam Lake, head to Cherrapunji via Laitlum Canyon, trek to the double decker root bridge at Nongriat with a guide, and visit Mawlynnong and Dawki before returning via Shnongpdeng and Jowai. Stays are split between Shillong, Cherrapunji and Dawki. Trips run every Friday, with groups usually between 8 and 50 travellers, many travelling solo.

faqs.q: What is the best time to visit Meghalaya?
faqs.a: October to April is great for sightseeing, and September to December is especially beautiful after the rains. Monsoon brings the biggest waterfalls but heavy rain.

faqs.q: How many days do I need for Meghalaya?
faqs.a: Five to seven days covers Shillong, Cherrapunji, the root bridges and Dawki comfortably. Our trip is 5 nights / 6 days.

faqs.q: Is the Nongriat root bridge trek difficult?
faqs.a: It involves a long flight of steps down to the village and back up, so a reasonable level of fitness helps. Take it at your own pace and wear shoes with good grip.

faqs.q: Where does the Meghalaya trip start and end?
faqs.a: It starts and ends in Guwahati, the main gateway to Meghalaya, and costs from ₹22,499 per person.

faqs.q: What should I pack for Meghalaya?
faqs.a: A rain jacket or umbrella, quick-dry clothes, a light warm layer for Shillong evenings and sturdy shoes with good grip for wet trails.

intro: Golden forts, desert dunes, lake palaces and royal history: Rajasthan weekend getaways to Jaisalmer and Udaipur.
content:
## Why go to Rajasthan
Rajasthan is India at its most royal. Massive forts, ornate palaces, carved havelis and colourful bazaars sit against a backdrop of desert and the Aravalli hills. In Jaisalmer, the golden fort is still lived in, and evenings at the Sam sand dunes end with folk music under the stars. Udaipur, the city of lakes, is all about Lake Pichola and the City Palace, while Kumbhalgarh's UNESCO-listed fort is famous for its enormous walls. Great food, warm hospitality and endless photo spots make it perfect for a short break.

## Best time to visit
October to March is the best time, with pleasant days and cool nights, especially in the desert. April to June is very hot. The monsoon brings some greenery, particularly around Udaipur.

## How to reach
Jaisalmer has a railway station and an airport with limited flights, and Jodhpur is another common gateway. Udaipur has Maharana Pratap Airport and a railway station. Both are popular overnight road journeys from Delhi NCR.

## Our Rajasthan trips
We run two Rajasthan weekend getaways. **Jaisalmer** is 2 nights / 3 days, starting from ₹7,499 per person, with a city tour of the fort and havelis, the Longewala battlefield and a stay in hotels and Swiss tents at the dunes with a bonfire and folk music. **Udaipur Kumbhalgarh** is 2 nights / 3 days, starting from ₹7,999 per person, travelling from Gurugram in an AC vehicle, with Udaipur sightseeing, Lake Pichola and the City Palace, and Kumbhalgarh Fort. Trips run every Friday, and groups usually have 8 to 50 travellers, many joining solo.

faqs.q: What is the best time to visit Rajasthan?
faqs.a: October to March, when days are pleasant and desert nights are cool. Summers are very hot.

faqs.q: Which Rajasthan trip should I choose?
faqs.a: Pick Jaisalmer (from ₹7,499 per person) for desert dunes, camp nights and the golden fort. Pick Udaipur Kumbhalgarh (from ₹7,999 per person) for lakes, palaces and a massive hill fort.

faqs.q: How many days do I need for a Rajasthan weekend trip?
faqs.a: Both our trips are 2 nights / 3 days, which is enough to see the highlights of one region over a long weekend.

faqs.q: Are these trips good for solo travellers?
faqs.a: Yes. Many of our travellers join solo, and weekend getaways are an easy way to try group travel for the first time.

faqs.q: What should I pack for Rajasthan?
faqs.a: Light cotton clothes for the day, a warm layer for desert nights in winter, sunscreen, sunglasses, a cap and comfortable walking shoes for forts.

intro: Snow-covered monasteries, frozen landscapes and cosy village homestays: Winter Spiti backpacking trips for the truly adventurous.
content:
## Why go to Spiti
Spiti Valley is a high-altitude cold desert in Himachal Pradesh, and in winter it becomes a silent white wonderland. Ancient monasteries like Key and Tabo sit under snow, villages such as Hikkim, Komic and Langza feel frozen in time, and the night skies are some of the clearest you will ever see. The road in winds through Kinnaur, past Sangla, Chitkul and Nako. This is raw, remote travel, and that is exactly the appeal.

## Best time to visit
Spiti can be visited in summer, roughly May to October, when both the Shimla and Manali routes are usually open. Winter, from about December to February, is for those who want snow and solitude, with very low temperatures and basic facilities. In winter the Manali side is closed, so travel is via Shimla and Kinnaur.

## How to reach
Shimla is the usual starting point for winter trips, with road connections from Delhi and Chandigarh. Chandigarh has the nearest major airport, and Shimla has a small airport and the toy train from Kalka.

## Our Spiti trips
Our **Winter Spiti** backpacking trip is 6 nights / 7 days, starting from ₹16,999 per person. It begins with an AC bus from Delhi to Shimla, then travels by tempo traveller through Sangla and Chitkul, Khab and Nako, to Chicham Bridge and Key Monastery, the villages of Hikkim, Komic and Langza, and back via Kaza and Kalpa. Stays in winter are mostly simple village homestays with hearty local food, and facilities like running water can be limited. Trips run every Friday, with groups usually between 8 and 50 travellers, many travelling solo.

faqs.q: When is the best time to visit Spiti?
faqs.a: Summer (roughly May to October) is easier travel, while winter (about December to February) is for snow, frozen landscapes and very few tourists.

faqs.q: Is Winter Spiti suitable for first-timers?
faqs.a: It is doable if you are prepared for extreme cold and basic stays. It suits travellers who want real adventure more than comfort. If you have any medical condition, check with your doctor before travelling to high altitude.

faqs.q: How many days do I need for Winter Spiti?
faqs.a: About a week, since the route via Shimla and Kinnaur is long. Our Winter Spiti trip is 6 nights / 7 days, starting from ₹16,999 per person.

faqs.q: What are the stays like in winter?
faqs.a: Most hotels close in winter, so stays are mainly village homestays. Expect simple, warm rooms, basic bathrooms and limited running water.

faqs.q: What should I pack for Winter Spiti?
faqs.a: Heavy down jacket, thermals, woollen socks, gloves, a warm cap, waterproof snow boots, sunglasses, sunscreen and lip balm.

intro: Island hopping by speedboat, Phi Phi, Krabi and Koh Samui nights: Thailand group trips packed with beaches and parties.
content:
## Why go to Thailand
Thailand is the classic first international trip for Indian travellers, and it never gets old. The Andaman coast around Phuket and Krabi is famous for limestone cliffs, turquoise water and island hopping, while Koh Samui in the Gulf of Thailand brings palm-lined beaches and a laid-back island feel. Add street food, night markets, temples like Wat Chalong and the Big Buddha in Phuket, and some of the best nightlife in Asia, and it is easy to see why groups love it.

## Best time to visit
November to April is the most popular season, with drier, sunnier weather on the Andaman coast. May to October is the rainy season on that side, with rougher seas on some days. Koh Samui follows a slightly different pattern, with its wettest months usually towards the end of the year.

## How to reach
Phuket International Airport is the main gateway for the islands, with direct and connecting flights from several Indian cities. Bangkok is the other major hub. Indian passport holders should check the current visa rules for Thailand well before travel.

## Our Thailand trips
Our **Thailand** trip is 6 nights / 7 days, starting from ₹44,499 per person. It starts in Phuket and moves to Krabi for a Four Island tour by speedboat, then on to Koh Samui for time on the island and a leisure day, back to Phuket by bus and ferry for a city walk and pub crawl, and a Phi Phi day trip by speedboat before departure from Phuket. Airport pick-up and drop at the destination city is included. Trips run every Friday, and groups usually have 8 to 50 travellers, many joining solo.

faqs.q: What is the best time to visit Thailand?
faqs.a: November to April is the most popular time for the beaches around Phuket and Krabi, with drier and sunnier weather.

faqs.q: Do Indians need a visa for Thailand?
faqs.a: Visa rules for Indian passport holders change from time to time, so please check the current rules with official sources well before your trip.

faqs.q: How many days are enough for Thailand?
faqs.a: A week is a good length to see a few islands without rushing. Our Thailand trip is 6 nights / 7 days, starting from ₹44,499 per person.

faqs.q: Which places does the Thailand trip cover?
faqs.a: Phuket, Krabi and Koh Samui, including a Four Island tour and a Phi Phi day trip by speedboat.

faqs.q: Is the Thailand trip good for solo travellers?
faqs.a: Yes. Many travellers join our international trips solo, and the island hopping and nights out make it easy to bond with the group.

faqs.q: What should I pack for Thailand?
faqs.a: Light summer clothes, swimwear, sunscreen, flip-flops, a light rain jacket and one modest outfit with covered shoulders and knees for temple visits.

intro: Himalayan views, snow at Auli, the Tungnath trek and easy weekend escapes from Delhi: Uttarakhand group trips for every kind of traveller.
content:
## Why go to Uttarakhand
Uttarakhand, the land of the gods, is the easiest way to swap Delhi's rush for the mountains. In a single weekend you can camp under pine forests, trek to one of the highest Shiva temples in the world at Tungnath, catch Himalayan views from Auli, or try water sports on Tehri Lake. Quieter hill towns like Chakrata and Mukteshwar offer waterfalls, caves, temples and fresh air, and Kainchi Dham draws visitors for its peaceful ashram. Whatever your vibe, there is a trip here for it.

## Best time to visit
March to June is pleasant and great for treks and sightseeing. October and November bring clear skies and crisp mountain views after the monsoon. December to February is snow season in higher places like Auli and Chopta. The monsoon, roughly July to September, can cause landslides on mountain roads.

## How to reach
Dehradun's Jolly Grant Airport and Pantnagar Airport serve the region, and Dehradun, Haridwar and Kathgodam are the main railheads. Most weekend trips are an overnight drive from Delhi.

## Our Uttarakhand trips
All our Uttarakhand trips are weekend getaways from Delhi, and they run every Friday:
- **Chakrata**, 1 night / 2 days, starting from ₹4,499 per person: Budher Caves trek, Tiger Falls and Chirmiri Neck Top.
- **Kanatal Tehri**, 1 night / 2 days, starting from ₹4,999 per person: camping at Kanatal, Surkanda Devi temple and water sports on Tehri Lake.
- **Mukteshwar**, 1 night / 2 days, starting from ₹4,999 per person: Mukteshwar temple, Chauli ki Jaali and Kainchi Dham.
- **Chopta Tungnath**, 2 nights / 3 days, starting from ₹6,199 per person: Tungnath and Chandrashila trek plus Deoria Tal.
- **Auli**, 2 nights / 3 days, starting from ₹7,999 per person: a day in Auli with the Gorson Bugyal trek.

Groups usually have 8 to 50 travellers, and many join solo.

faqs.q: What is the best time to visit Uttarakhand?
faqs.a: March to June and October to November are great for treks and views. Come in December to February if you want snow at places like Auli and Chopta.

faqs.q: Which Uttarakhand trip should I choose?
faqs.a: For a short, easy break pick Chakrata (from ₹4,499), Kanatal Tehri or Mukteshwar (from ₹4,999). For a trek pick Chopta Tungnath (from ₹6,199), and for snow and big Himalayan views pick Auli (from ₹7,999).

faqs.q: How many days do I need?
faqs.a: A weekend is enough. Our Uttarakhand trips are either 1 night / 2 days or 2 nights / 3 days, leaving from Delhi.

faqs.q: Is the Chopta Tungnath trek good for beginners?
faqs.a: Yes, it is a popular beginner-friendly trek. The trail is well marked, though it is steady uphill, so take it at your own pace.

faqs.q: Are these trips good for solo travellers?
faqs.a: Yes. Weekend getaways are a great first group trip, and many of our travellers join solo.

faqs.q: What should I pack for Uttarakhand?
faqs.a: Warm layers (nights get cold even in summer), a jacket, comfortable trekking shoes, a rain layer and basic toiletries. In winter add thermals, gloves and a woollen cap.

intro: Halong Bay cruises, Hoi An's lantern-lit old town, Ba Na Hills and Hanoi's Train Street: Vietnam group trips from south to north.
content:
## Why go to Vietnam
Vietnam packs a whole world into one long, narrow country. In the south, Ho Chi Minh City buzzes with scooters, street food and history at the Cu Chi Tunnels. In the centre, Da Nang has long beaches and the Dragon Bridge, Ba Na Hills has the famous Golden Bridge held up by giant stone hands, and Hoi An's ancient town glows with lanterns at night. Up north, Hanoi's Old Quarter and Train Street lead on to Halong Bay, with its limestone islands rising out of emerald water. Add great coffee and pho, and it is an easy country to fall for.

## Best time to visit
Vietnam's weather varies by region. Spring, roughly February to April, and autumn, around September to November, are generally pleasant across much of the country. The north gets cool in winter, and central Vietnam sees heavy rain later in the year.

## How to reach
Ho Chi Minh City and Hanoi are the main international gateways, with Da Nang serving the centre. Flights from India usually connect via these cities. Indian passport holders should check the current visa rules for Vietnam before travel.

## Our Vietnam trips
Our **Vietnam** trip is 7 nights / 8 days, starting from ₹44,499 per person. It runs south to north: Ho Chi Minh City and the Cu Chi Tunnels with the War Remnants Museum, Da Nang's beaches and Dragon Bridge, Ba Na Hills by cable car, a bamboo basket boat ride and Hoi An's ancient town with a lantern boat ride, Hanoi's Old Quarter, Train Street and Beer Street, and a Halong Bay cruise with kayaking, cave exploration and an overnight stay. Trips run every Friday, and groups usually have 8 to 50 travellers, many joining solo.

faqs.q: What is the best time to visit Vietnam?
faqs.a: Spring (around February to April) and autumn (around September to November) are generally pleasant, but weather differs between the north, centre and south.

faqs.q: Do Indians need a visa for Vietnam?
faqs.a: Yes, Indian passport holders need a visa for Vietnam, and the rules can change. Check the current requirements on official sources before you travel.

faqs.q: How many days are enough for Vietnam?
faqs.a: About a week to ten days lets you cover the south, centre and north. Our Vietnam trip is 7 nights / 8 days, starting from ₹44,499 per person.

faqs.q: Which places does the Vietnam trip cover?
faqs.a: Ho Chi Minh City, the Cu Chi Tunnels, Da Nang, Ba Na Hills, Hoi An, Hanoi and an overnight Halong Bay cruise.

faqs.q: Is Vietnam good for solo travellers?
faqs.a: Yes. Vietnam is a popular and friendly destination, and many travellers join our group trips solo.

faqs.q: What should I pack for Vietnam?
faqs.a: Light breathable clothes, a light jacket for the north and the Halong Bay cruise, a rain layer, comfortable walking shoes and swimwear for Da Nang.
